analytical_question: Should this conservative delivery fleet proceed with a near-term grid-export trial while protecting daily route readiness?
general_et_finding: V2G is technically feasible with capable vehicles and charging equipment, but technical capability does not establish broad commercial diffusion. DOE distinguishes grid export from V2B backup and notes that vehicle grid-service incentive programs are not widely available. ([energy.gov](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging))
application_finding: The proposed use requires actual grid export, not merely backup power or managed charging; DOE identifies utility interconnection permission as relevant. Application-specific inference: discharge controls must preserve departure charge because unexpected depletion could prevent deliveries. ([energy.gov](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging))
organization_specific_finding: Hypothetical assumptions establish written pilot permission and compatible trial hardware, but not documented warranty coverage or commercial terms. Those unresolved prerequisites—not conservative appetite alone—block exposing route vehicles to this trial.

evidence.claim: DOE distinguishes V2B backup from V2G export and advises checking utility permission for reverse power flow.
evidence.source_or_reference: U.S. Department of Energy, FEMP, Managed and Bidirectional Charging. ([energy.gov](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging))
evidence.date_or_recency: Page undated; verified during this run. Case packet reports retrieval on October 13, 2026.
evidence.notes: Supports general prerequisites, not permission, warranty coverage, or commercial viability for this hypothetical fleet.

evidence.claim: DOE describes managed charging as accounting for vehicle energy needs and states that V2G incentive programs are not widely in place.
evidence.source_or_reference: U.S. Department of Energy, FEMP, Managed and Bidirectional Charging. ([energy.gov](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging))
evidence.date_or_recency: Page undated; verified during this run.
evidence.notes: Supports separating technical capability from diffusion and considering managed charging; it does not establish local savings.

evidence.claim: The fleet has assumed trial permission and compatible hardware but will not expose route vehicles without documented warranty and commercial terms.
evidence.notes: Not observations of a real organization or field-deployment evidence.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Counter-case: assumed permission and compatible hardware make a bounded experiment plausible once warranty and commercial prerequisites are resolved; the evidence does not justify rejecting V2G outright.
The undated DOE guidance does not establish current local market availability, fleet-specific battery effects, or profitable operation.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence in deferral under the stated organizational constraint; limited confidence in eventual commercial value. No fleet-specific warranty, contract, or route-reserve validation evidence is supplied.
value_opportunity_implication: The strongest near-term alternative is ordinary managed charging, which DOE describes as accommodating vehicle energy needs without requiring grid export. Inference: it offers a lower-consequence learning path, but no fleet-specific savings are established. ([energy.gov](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging))
risk_governance_implication: Before route-vehicle participation, require documented export-related warranty coverage and commercial obligations, plus validated departure-charge protection, human stop authority, and a reversible return to charging-only operation. Pass operating capacity and implementation ownership to the Organizational Adoption Agent.
recommendation_management_implication: Defer. Missing warranty and commercial documentation is the decisive blocker; reverse to a bounded experiment only when those terms are accepted and route-reserve safeguards are validated within the assumed permitted configuration.
change_monitoring_triggers: Manufacturer documentation establishes warranty treatment for the exact vehicle, equipment, and grid-export use.
Written commercial terms establish compensation, costs, dispatch obligations, and exit rights acceptable to the fleet.
Controlled testing validates departure-charge protection and human override; together with accepted documentation, this supports reconsideration as a bounded experiment.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Provide the vehicle-specific warranty documentation and proposed commercial agreement; without them, do not authorize route-vehicle grid export.
Provide route energy requirements and reserve-control test evidence before judging delivery-readiness protection.
